inputs.share_count_basis: diluted weighted-average shares, back-solved from Q3 FY2026 10-Q net income $362M / diluted EPS $1.28 = 283M; held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in owner FCF (charging both would double-count per section 1 of owner-fcf.md)
inputs.sbc_source: TTM (FY2025 - 9M-2025 + 9M-2026) of cash-flow-statement SBC add-back ($130M) plus cash taxes withheld on equity-award net-share settlement ($32M, the equity_award_taxes KPI), summed because Agilent's 10-K does not publish one combined adjusted-EBITDA reconciliation line for this item; see A.duckdb kpis table (equity_award_taxes, FY2025=29, 9M-2025=28, 9M-2026=31)
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-24T20:02:58Z regular close (Yahoo Finance chart API); 52-week range 108.35-174.77
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9% nominal USD WACC: ~4.2% risk-free (10yr UST), ~5.5% ERP, beta ~1.05 for a moderately cyclical life-sciences-instruments compounder, blended with a small after-tax cost of debt on ~1.0x EBITDA net leverage. Same WACC used across all three scenarios -- risk is expressed in the diverging cash-flow paths and probability weights, not stacked again as a discount-rate premium (owner-fcf.md section 7g).
inputs.lease_treatment: not material -- Agilent's operating leases are small relative to the balance sheet (life-sciences instrument manufacturer with owned facilities); no separate lease adjustment applied
inputs.nci_treatment: none -- Agilent has no reported non-controlling interests
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, scenario-weighted (.claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md routing: profitable US operating company, life-sciences/diagnostics instruments and consumables -- the default owner-FCF route, no adaptations file needed since USD-only, no leases/NCI/non-operating assets of consequence). FIRST valuation of this ticker (no memory entry, no prior DCF/Drivers file). Base year is a TTM reconstruction (FY2025 - 9M FY2025 + 9M FY2026) rather than the last completed FY2025, because Q3 FY2026 (ended 2026-07-31, reported 2026-08-26) is materially fresher and captures the recent China re-acceleration (+9% vs flat expected) and raised FY2026 guidance. Interest income NOT stripped from owner FCF: Agilent carries net DEBT (~$1,887M, ~1.0x TTM EBITDA), not net cash -- the double-count this adjustment guards against (adding a cash pile to EV while also leaving its income in FCF) does not arise here, since net debt is SUBTRACTED from EV, not added. Cash tax rate held flat at 21% across all years and scenarios: FY2024/FY2025 cash-tax-paid/EBIT ran 21.1%/21.5%, a normal statutory-blend rate with no valuation-allowance release or one-off credit to ramp away from (FY2023's lower 14.7% was the outlier, not the recent years, so no ramp applied). shareholders_equity for FY2023 in the DB (-327) is a data-extraction error -- FY2023 total_assets (10,763) minus total_liabilities (4,918) implies equity of ~5,845, consistent with the Q1-Q3 2023 progression and the FY2024 opening balance; not used as a CAGR endpoint so it does not affect historical_growth, but flagging for a future make-fix pass. Buyback cash ($295M in 9M FY2026) funds the flat share count -- Agilent is an active repurchaser, so the flat count is a funded convention, not an unpaid one. Stock trades near its 52-week high ($172.84 vs 108.35-174.77 range) on a beat-and-raise Q3 FY2026 print; EV/TTM-EBITDA ~26.6x and TTM P/E ~37x are rich for a moderately cyclical instruments/diagnostics business, which is the central tension this DCF surfaces -- see valuation_philosophy.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 5yr CAGR (14.72%) is far above equity 5yr CAGR (6.71%) and revenue 5yr CAGR (5.41%), driven mainly by FY2018's depressed base (a one-off $320M-plus tax item cut FY2018 EPS to $0.97) rather than a genuine acceleration in per-share value creation; equity and revenue CAGRs, which are not distorted by that base effect, are used to anchor the growth path instead of EPS. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (6.72%) is barely below reported-FCF 5yr CAGR (7.51%), so SBC is growing only modestly faster than cash flow -- not the large gap seen in heavy-SBC tech names.
historical_growth.notes: FY2023 shareholders_equity in the DB (-327) is a data-extraction error (assets-minus-liabilities imply ~5,845); not used as an endpoint here, so equity CAGRs above are unaffected. All CAGR endpoints (FY2020, FY2022, FY2025) are clean cross-checked figures.

base.narrative: Core organic growth decelerates from FY2026 guidance (~6% core) toward a long-run ~3% as the current tailwinds (GLP-1/CDMO biologics testing, pharma reshoring, China's Q3 re-acceleration) mature and instrument-cycle growth reverts to its historical mid-single-digit norm. EBITDA margin expands steadily from ~26.3% toward ~29% at maturity, consistent with management's guided pricing power (>100bps/yr) and continued mix-shift toward CrossLab consumables/services and CDMO. SBC declines modestly as a share of revenue as recent large-M&A-related equity grants roll off. Working capital consumes a modest 5% of each year's revenue growth (receivables/inventory build against a smaller consumables-heavy payables base), and cash tax holds at the recent 21% run-rate with no assumed credit or relief.

bull.narrative: GLP-1/biologics CDMO demand (Advanced Therapeutics +30% and GLP-1 testing +70% YoY in Q3 FY2026) proves durable rather than a one-time step-up, China's re-acceleration (+9% vs flat expected) persists through year-end and beyond, and the ~$1B pharma-reshoring opportunity through 2030 lands ahead of schedule as Agilent captures orders from more of the top-10 global pharma companies. BIOVECTRA and Biocare Medical integrate cleanly, pricing power holds above the 100bp guided floor, and mix shift toward CrossLab/CDMO pushes EBITDA margin into the low-30s at maturity -- a Danaher/Thermo-like margin profile.

bear.narrative: China's Q3 FY2026 strength reverses (the business has swung from flat-expected to +9% and back before on stimulus/tender timing), NIH and academic/government funding cuts bite harder into a historically stable customer base, and biopharma R&D spending outside GLP-1-linked programs stays muted. BIOVECTRA integration -- already flagged by trade press as 'a work in progress' -- disappoints, and Biocare Medical's contribution stalls. Europe stays soft on delayed capex, and the ~$20M/quarter tariff-refund tailwind that flattered recent EPS does not persist, exposing a lower underlying margin base. Growth settles near 2-2.5% and margin expansion stalls in the mid-24% range.

scenario_narratives.base: Guidance-consistent deceleration: FY2026 core growth (~6%) fades toward a ~3% long-run rate as GLP-1/CDMO, reshoring and China tailwinds normalize; margin keeps expanding on pricing and mix but at a moderating pace.
scenario_narratives.bull: GLP-1/CDMO, China and reshoring tailwinds all persist and compound; BIOVECTRA/Biocare integrate cleanly; margin reaches a Danaher/Thermo-like low-30s ceiling.
scenario_narratives.bear: China re-accelerates and then reverses again as it has historically; NIH/academic funding and Europe capex stay weak; recent M&A integration disappoints; tariff-refund tailwind fades, exposing a lower underlying margin.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Standard base weight. Bear raised slightly above the 15% house default (to 20%) because China's Q3 re-acceleration has reversed on Agilent before and the two largest near-term tailwinds (China, tariff refunds) are both explicitly flagged by management as non-repeating in their own current-quarter guidance -- this is a real, not hypothetical, downside path. Bull trimmed to 30% because it requires GLP-1/CDMO, China, reshoring AND clean M&A integration to all continue simultaneously; no single catalyst on its own gets the stock to today's price in this model.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Agilent is a high-quality, moderately cyclical life-sciences instrumentation and consumables business with a large recurring CrossLab annuity (>40% of revenue) that dampens the instrument-capex cycle, augmented by GLP-1/biologics CDMO and pharma-reshoring growth vectors. The owner-FCF DCF here -- built from components off a fresh TTM base through Q3 FY2026, margin still maturing over a 10-year horizon, and a 9% WACC applied uniformly across scenarios -- values even the bull case (all growth and margin tailwinds sustained) at roughly two-thirds of the current $172.84 price, with a probability-weighted intrinsic value well below that. The gap is not a quality problem with the business; it is that the stock trades at rich multiples (EV/TTM-EBITDA ~26.6x, TTM P/E ~37x) near its 52-week high following a beat-and-raise Q3 print, pricing in sustained double-digit CDMO growth, a persistent China recovery and continued margin expansion toward levels this model treats as a bull-case outcome, not a base case.
key_risks_to_valuation: China revenue is genuinely volatile (flat-expected to +9% swing in one quarter); if the model's bear case is closer to the truth than base, downside from here is significant
BIOVECTRA and Biocare Medical integration risk -- trade press already flags BIOVECTRA as 'a work in progress' two years post-close
NIH/academic government funding policy is a real, ongoing headwind to a historically stable customer base
Roughly $20M/quarter of recent EPS benefit came from tariff refunds that FY2026 guidance already nets out of Q4 -- underlying ex-tariff growth is more moderate than headline prints suggest
The valuation gap versus the market price could close via multiple compression (a normal risk for any DCF on a richly-priced quality name) rather than the business underperforming operationally
